'''''Clutia pulchella''''', the '''lightning bush''', is a southern African [[dioecious]] [[shrub]] of the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Peraceae]]. It occurs at middle altitudes in Namibia, Mozambique,<ref name=pd>{{cite web |title=''Clutia pulchella'' |work=Plant Database |url=http://www.plantdatabase.co.uk/Clutia_pulchella |accessdate=2 January 2013 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20131015093059/http://www.plantdatabase.co.uk/Clutia_pulchella |archive-date=15 October 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Zimbabwe,<ref name=fz>{{cite web |last=Hyde |first=M. A. |title=''Clutia pulchella'' L. var. ''obtusata'' Sond. |url=http://www.zimbabweflora.co.zw/speciesdata/species.php?species_id=135600 |work=Flora of Zimbabwe |accessdate=2 January 2013|display-authors=etal}}</ref> Eswatini,<ref name=sfd>{{cite web|title=''Clutia pulchella'' L. var. ''pulchella''|url=http://www.sntc.org.sz/flora/speciesinfo.asp?spid=1699 |work=Swaziland's Flora Database |publisher=SNTC |accessdate=2 January 2013}}</ref> Botswana, Lesotho and South Africa.<ref name=apd>{{cite web |title=''Clutia pulchella'' L. |url=http://www.ville-ge.ch/musinfo/bd/cjb/africa/details.php?langue=an&id=174049 |work=African Plant Database |publisher=CJB & SANBI |accessdate=2 January 2013}}</ref>

==Description==
They may grow {{convert|2|-|3|m|ft}} high,<ref name=sfd/> and occur on a variety of broken terrain types.

The twigs are green with some wart-like growths. Leaf shape is somewhat variable, either blunt-tipped ovate or broadly lanceolate. The foliage is bluish-green but sometimes interspersed with some bright orange leaves.<ref name=vw>{{cite book |last=Van Wyk |first=Braam |title=Veldgids tot die Veldblomme van die Witwatersrand- en Pretoria-gebied |year=1988 |publisher=Struik |location=Cape Town |isbn=0-86977-815-3 |pages=130–131}}</ref> They are soft with venation that is transparent against light, besides the numerous glands that dot each leaf.<ref name=vw/><ref group="Note">i.e. punctate with pellucid glands, or pellucid-punctate.</ref>

The axillary flowers develop into spherical,<ref name=sfd/> clearly three-chambered capsules. The capsules are about {{convert|3|mm}} in diameter, and may bear warts. Seeds are released when the dry capsules burst open.

It is a food plant for the [[Chrysoritis aureus|Heidelberg copper]] butterfly. It is similar to the related [[monoecious]] species ''[[Clutia abyssinica|C. abyssinica]]'', which has the leaves more elongated.<ref name=apd/>
